```{r}
print(headers)
length(headers)
```

## My FASTA Output

```{r}
sample_id_pattern <- "([\\w-]+)"                
organism_pattern  <- "H.\\w+\\s?\\w+s"     #og is "H(.\\w+)"           
gene_pattern      <- "([BTE][\\w]+)" 

extracted <- data.frame(
  header    = headers,
  sample_id = str_extract(headers, sample_id_pattern),
  organism  = str_extract(headers, organism_pattern),
  gene      = str_match(headers, gene_pattern)[, 2],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
extracted
```

## AI FASTA Output - Claude Sonnet 5.5

```{r}
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# parse_fasta.R
# Parse a messy FASTA file (inconsistent header formats) into a table.
# Values are pulled exactly as they appear in the header (no standardizing).
# Base R only, no packages required.
#
# Usage: Rscript parse_fasta.R [input.fasta] [output.csv]

args     <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
in_file  <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else "messy_sequences.fasta"
out_file <- if (length(args) >= 2) args[2] else "clean_sequences.csv"

# ---- helper: first capture group of a perl regex, NA if no match -----------
extract1 <- function(x, pattern) {
  m <- regexec(pattern, x, perl = TRUE)
  vapply(seq_along(x), function(i) {
    g <- regmatches(x[i], m[i])[[1]]
    if (length(g) >= 2) g[2] else NA_character_
  }, character(1))
}

# ---- 1. Read file and group lines into records -----------------------------
lines <- trimws(readLines(in_file, warn = FALSE))
lines <- lines[nzchar(lines)]

is_header <- grepl("^>", lines)
if (!any(is_header)) stop("No FASTA headers (lines starting with '>') found.")
record_id <- cumsum(is_header)

headers <- sub("^>\\s*", "", lines[is_header])   # full header, no leading '>'

seq_lines <- lines[!is_header & record_id > 0]
seq_ids   <- record_id[!is_header & record_id > 0]
seqs      <- tapply(seq_lines, seq_ids,
                    function(x) paste(gsub("\\s", "", x), collapse = ""))
sequence  <- unname(seqs[as.character(seq_along(headers))])
sequence[is.na(sequence)] <- ""

# ---- 2. Sample ID (first token, exactly as written) ------------------------
# Everything up to the first whitespace, '|' or ';'
sample_id <- extract1(headers, "^([^\\s|;]+)")

# ---- 3. Organism (exactly as written) --------------------------------------
# (a) keyed: organism=... / organism:... / species=... / species:...
#     value runs until the next "key=" / "key:", a '|' or ';', or end of line
organism_key <- trimws(extract1(
  headers,
  "(?i)\\b(?:organism|species)\\s*[=:]\\s*(.+?)(?=\\s+\\w+\\s*[=:]|\\s*[|;]|$)"))

# (b) unkeyed: recognise Homo sapiens / Homo_sapiens / H.sapiens / Hsapiens
org_pattern <- "(?i)\\b(Homo[_ ]?sapiens|H\\.\\s?sapiens|Hsapiens)\\b"
organism_pos <- extract1(headers, org_pattern)

organism <- ifelse(is.na(organism_key), organism_pos, organism_key)

# ---- 4. Gene (exactly as written) ------------------------------------------
# (a) keyed: gene=BRCA1, gene:TP53, target=BRCA1
gene_key <- extract1(headers, "(?i)\\b(?:gene|target)\\s*[=:]\\s*([^\\s|;]+)")

# (b) positional fallback: drop the ID and organism, split what is left on
#     | ; whitespace, and take the first token that looks like a gene symbol
#     (capital letter, then capitals/digits, 2-10 chars; no '=' or ':').
gene_positional <- vapply(seq_along(headers), function(i) {
  rest   <- sub("^[^\\s|;]+", "", headers[i], perl = TRUE)   # drop ID
  rest   <- gsub(org_pattern, " ", rest, perl = TRUE)        # drop organism
  tokens <- strsplit(rest, "[|;[:space:]]+", perl = TRUE)[[1]]
  hit    <- tokens[grepl("^[A-Z][A-Z0-9-]{1,9}$", tokens)]
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
}, character(1))

gene <- ifelse(is.na(gene_key), gene_positional, gene_key)

# ---- 5. Assemble the table -------------------------------------------------
clean <- data.frame(
  header     = headers,
  sample_id  = sample_id,
  organism   = organism,
  gene       = gene,
  seq_length = nchar(sequence),
  sequence   = sequence,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# ---- 6. Sanity checks ------------------------------------------------------
for (col in c("sample_id", "organism", "gene")) {
  bad <- which(is.na(clean[[col]]))
  if (length(bad))
    warning(sprintf("Could not parse '%s' for record(s): %s",
                    col, paste(bad, collapse = ", ")))
}

print(clean[, c("sample_id", "organism", "gene", "seq_length", "header")],
      row.names = FALSE, right = FALSE)

write.csv(clean, out_file, row.names = FALSE)
message("\nWrote ", nrow(clean), " records to ", out_file)
```

## Cleaning the Table

```{r}
samples <- read.csv("messy_samples.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
samples[13, 'sex']
samples[samples == ""] <- NA
```

## My Table Output

```{r}
samples2 <- samples %>%
  mutate(
    clean_sample_id = str_remove(
        str_replace(sample_id, "^s", "S"),
        "\\-"
    ),
    
    clean_dob = dob %>%
    str_replace_all("\\.", "/") %>%
    parse_date_time(orders = c("mdy", "ymd", "dby")) %>%
    as.Date(),
    
    clean_sex = sex %>%
      str_replace("Female|f", "F") %>%
      str_replace("m|Male", "M") %>%
      str_replace("unknown", "U") %>%
      replace_na("U"),
    
    clean_enrollment_site = str_replace(str_replace(str_replace(str_replace(str_replace(
      enrollment_site, "ITE-", "ite "), "s", "S"), "eB", "e B"), "_a", " A"), "  ", " "
    )) %>%
    
    filter(
    str_to_lower(glucose_unit) != "mmol/l",
    !is.na(glucose_value),
    glucose_value != "N/A"
    ) %>%
  
    mutate(
      clean_glucose_value = str_remove(
        glucose_value, "\\*"
      ),
      
      clean_glucose_unit = str_replace(
        glucose_unit, "MG/DL|mg/dl", "mg/dL"
      ),
      
      clean_patient_name = str_replace(str_replace(
        patient_name, "KIM", "Kim"), "DAVIS", "Davis"
      )
    
    )

samples2 <- samples2 %>%
  select(
    sample_id = clean_sample_id,
    glucose_value = clean_glucose_value,
    glucose_unit = clean_glucose_unit,
    patient_name = clean_patient_name,
    dob = clean_dob,
    sex = clean_sex,
    enrollment_site = clean_enrollment_site,
    notes
  )

```

## AI Table Output - Claude Sonnet 5.5

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# clean_samples.R
# Parse messy_samples.csv into a clean, consistent table using regex.
# Base R only (no packages required).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Read the raw data (everything as character so nothing is silently coerced)
ai_samples <- read.csv("messy_samples.csv",
                    colClasses = "character",
                    na.strings = character(0),
                    check.names = FALSE)

# Collapse runs of whitespace and trim ends ("Site  C " -> "Site C")
clean_ws <- function(x) trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", x))

# Capitalise the first letter of each word, lowercase the rest ("KIM" -> "Kim")
title_case <- function(x) gsub("\\b([a-z])", "\\U\\1", tolower(x), perl = TRUE)

# 2. sample_id: "s-0003" / "S0003" -> "S0003" ---------------------------------
sample_id <- toupper(clean_ws(ai_samples$sample_id))
sample_id <- sub("^S-?(\\d+)$", "S\\1", sample_id)

# 3. patient_name: "J. KIM" -> first_initial "J", last_name "Kim" -------------
name          <- clean_ws(ai_samples$patient_name)
name_re       <- "^([A-Za-z])\\.?\\s*(.+)$"
has_name      <- grepl(name_re, name)
first_initial <- ifelse(has_name, toupper(sub(name_re, "\\1", name)), NA)
last_name     <- ifelse(has_name, title_case(sub(name_re, "\\2", name)), NA)

# 4. dob -> ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) ----------------------------------------------
# Formats found: YYYY-MM-DD | MM/DD/YYYY | MM.DD.YY | DD-Mon-YYYY
# Slash and dot dates are treated as month-first (e.g. 12/16/1974, 11.24.53).
# Two-digit years are placed in the most recent century that isn't in the future.
parse_dob <- function(x, pivot_year = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"))) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  n <- length(x)
  yr <- mo <- dy <- rep(NA_integer_, n)
  done <- two_digit <- rep(FALSE, n)

  formats <- list(
    list(re = "^(\\d{4})-(\\d{1,2})-(\\d{1,2})$",          order = c("y", "m", "d")),
    list(re = "^(\\d{1,2})/(\\d{1,2})/(\\d{2}|\\d{4})$",   order = c("m", "d", "y")),
    list(re = "^(\\d{1,2})\\.(\\d{1,2})\\.(\\d{2}|\\d{4})$", order = c("m", "d", "y")),
    list(re = "^(\\d{1,2})-([A-Za-z]{3})-(\\d{2}|\\d{4})$", order = c("d", "m", "y"))
  )

  for (f in formats) {
    hit <- !done & grepl(f$re, x)
    if (!any(hit)) next
    comp <- setNames(
      lapply(1:3, function(i) sub(f$re, paste0("\\", i), x[hit])),
      f$order
    )
    mon <- comp$m
    mon_num <- ifelse(grepl("^[A-Za-z]+$", mon),
                      match(tolower(mon), tolower(month.abb)),
                      suppressWarnings(as.integer(mon)))
    two_digit[hit] <- nchar(comp$y) == 2
    yr[hit]   <- as.integer(comp$y)
    mo[hit]   <- as.integer(mon_num)
    dy[hit]   <- as.integer(comp$d)
    done[hit] <- TRUE
  }

  # Resolve two-digit years: 53 -> 1953, 02 -> 2002, etc.
  idx <- two_digit & !is.na(yr)
  yr[idx] <- ifelse(2000L + yr[idx] > pivot_year, 1900L + yr[idx], 2000L + yr[idx])

  out <- as.Date(sprintf("%04d-%02d-%02d", yr, mo, dy), format = "%Y-%m-%d")
  bad <- x != "" & is.na(out)
  if (any(bad)) warning("Unparsed dates: ", paste(x[bad], collapse = ", "))
  out
}
dob <- parse_dob(ai_samples$dob)

# 5. sex -> Female / Male / Unknown --------------------------------------------
s <- tolower(clean_ws(ai_samples$sex))
sex <- ifelse(grepl("^(f|female)$", s), "Female",
       ifelse(grepl("^(m|male)$",   s), "Male", "Unknown"))   # u, unknown, blank

# 6. enrollment_site: "SITE-A", "site_a", "siteB", "Site  C " -> "Site A/B/C" ---
site_re <- "^site[ _-]*([a-z])$"
s <- tolower(clean_ws(ai_samples$enrollment_site))
enrollment_site <- ifelse(grepl(site_re, s),
                          paste("Site", toupper(sub(site_re, "\\1", s))), NA)

# 7. glucose: numeric value (+ trailing "*" flag), standardise unit to mg/dL ---
raw    <- clean_ws(ai_samples$glucose_value)
num_re <- "^(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*(\\*?)$"
ok     <- grepl(num_re, raw, perl = TRUE)                    # "N/A" -> not ok
value  <- as.numeric(ifelse(ok, sub(num_re, "\\1", raw, perl = TRUE), NA))
glucose_flagged <- ok & grepl("\\*$", raw)                   # e.g. "112.3*"

u <- tolower(gsub("\\s+", "", ai_samples$glucose_unit))
unit <- ifelse(grepl("^mg/?dl$",   u), "mg/dL",
        ifelse(grepl("^mmol/?l$",  u), "mmol/L", NA))

MMOL_TO_MGDL <- 18.016                                       # 1 mmol/L glucose = 18.016 mg/dL
glucose_mg_dl <- round(ifelse(unit == "mg/dL",  value,
                       ifelse(unit == "mmol/L", value * MMOL_TO_MGDL, NA)), 1)

# Sanity check on the standardised values (plausible blood glucose: 20-600 mg/dL)
glucose_qc <- ifelse(is.na(glucose_mg_dl), "missing",
              ifelse(glucose_mg_dl < 20 | glucose_mg_dl > 600, "out_of_range", "ok"))

# 8. notes: blank -> NA, lowercase, trimmed -------------------------------------
notes <- tolower(clean_ws(ai_samples$notes))
notes[notes == ""] <- NA

# 9. Assemble the clean table -----------------------------------------------------
clean_samples <- data.frame(
  sample_id       = sample_id,
  first_initial   = first_initial,
  last_name       = last_name,
  dob             = dob,                 # Date, prints as YYYY-MM-DD
  sex             = sex,
  enrollment_site = enrollment_site,
  glucose_mg_dl   = glucose_mg_dl,
  glucose_orig_unit = unit,              # unit as originally reported
  glucose_flagged = glucose_flagged,     # TRUE if the raw value carried a "*"
  glucose_qc      = glucose_qc,
  notes           = notes,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Categorical columns as factors for downstream modelling/summaries
clean_samples$sex             <- factor(clean_samples$sex, levels = c("Female", "Male", "Unknown"))
clean_samples$enrollment_site <- factor(clean_samples$enrollment_site, levels = c("Site A", "Site B", "Site C"))

# 10. Inspect and save ------------------------------------------------------------
str(clean_samples)
print(head(clean_samples, 10))
print(table(clean_samples$glucose_qc, clean_samples$glucose_orig_unit, useNA = "ifany"))

# write.csv(clean_samples, "clean_samples.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
```
